Clean and replenish all dispensers
Flush the toilet before spraying with a sanitary All-Purpose cleaner inside the toilet as well as the outside and the pipes at the back
Spray the shower, bath, tiles and basin with the same chemical as the above
Treating of visible blood or bodily fluids first and clean before you continue with the rest of the cleaning
Use a green lavette cloth and green scourer pad to clean with a bathroom cleaner
Start cleaning the shower, shower doors, shower curtains, bath and all tiles, drains and overflows
Taps and spray heads free from lime scale
Wash and sanitise your hands before putting on the red household gloves for cleaning the toilet
Use your toilet brush if you see any visible mess
Rinse the toilet brush by flushing the toilet water once again
Shake off excess water from the toilet brush and spray brush with sanitiser
Toilet brush holder must be clean and sanitised
Use green scourer pad with your toilet bowl cleaner to remove all lime scale and marks underneath rim and where water flow comes into the toilet (Rim of the toilet must be free from any lime scale)
Use red lavette cloth and detergent to clean and wipe toilet clean on the outside and beneath and the pipes behind
Wash and sanitise your red gloves before you put in back on the trolley (gloves can be used until it is no longer safe to do so)
Spray toilet with sanitiser after cleaning and let it dry
Clean basin inside, outside and underneath where there are pipes
Correct use of masslin: changing cloths frequently, using one room cloths/ blue in wards, theatre, using yellow cloths in passage, use sweeping technique correctly
Clean basin outlet and overflow
Bathroom floors should be mopped with a damp flat mop and detergent
Complete your checklist behind the door
Wash and sanitise hands before putting protective cloth / or starting with work
Clean and replenish all paper, soaps sanitiser dispensers
Empty general refuse bin and replace plastic bags with the correct bin liner
Replace red bag with a new bag and discard full red bag
Start with high dusting and then to your lower areas
Clean and dust with a blue lavette cloth, blue bucket with detergent in your water
Wash Mattress with detergent and spray with sanitiser and leave to dry

Spray all washed areas with sanitiser after it has been cleaned and wipe door handles with sanitiser
Damped washed floor with detergent and dispose of dirty water in sluice
Complete room checklist that is thoroughly cleaned and sanitised
Control checks should be performed to ensure that the company cleaners use appropriate disinfectant solution to prevent the growth of any germs and funguses
General waste will be discarded in a clear / smoky bag in the yellow rubber bag of the trolley, which must have a clear bag in it for all the rubbish
Remove medical waste in the red bags with your red rubber gloves
Red bins must be clearly marked with Hospital name, ward no / named and dated
Full red bins will be stored and removed by reputable red waste movers who will discard waste as per government laws
Syringes and needles and medical bottles discarded in small yellow bucket
Ward name and date on needle container with an expiry date of 90 days or sooner
Drip pipes and drip bags and medicine bottles will be discarded in a yellow drum with red lid. also marked with name and dates

Normal dirty linen is transported i laundry trolley
Isolation linen and linen with bodily fluids must be bagged in a yellow bag
Theater and or blood stained linen must be in a red bag
Blood must be soaked in cold water and treated with a blood stain remover
Blood linen can go through into machine for normal wash, but after the blood stains have been removed
Isolation linen is only washed after all other linen has been washed, cleaned out of the laundry
A clean container is used to handle washed and dried linen. Clean linen is transported to wards in clean, closed containers or covered carts
